meta.tagline: Glenville NY · inpatient addiction treatment · Capital Region
meta.author: Aleksandar Spasevski
meta.doc_subtitle: Glenville leads its local Map Pack and is gaining · organic conversion rate roughly doubled Q3 '25 to Q1 '26 · main service pages capped by a single-city URL · Google Business depth on the Glenville pin · site cleanup

yoy_fallback_html: YoY comparisons aren't meaningful here — Q1–Q2 2025 were the migration gap (near-zero traffic). See the quarterly trajectory below for the post-recovery picture: sessions softening as the older blog cluster loses rankings, but organic conversion rate roughly doubled (0.39% Q3 '25 → 0.94% Q1 '26) and form-submit lead volume held steady.
tldr: The Glenville location is winning where it counts. Conifer Park's Glenville pin holds the top of its local Map Pack and is still gaining: it added 19 top-3 grid cells this period and is #1 at the facility across the core searches. Google Business and Maps clicks climbed from about 700 a month to a March peak of 1,099, and the people arriving convert better than before (organic conversion rate roughly doubled, Q3 2025 0.39% to Q1 2026 0.94%), so form-submit leads held steady even as the older blog pages slipped. The clearest gains left are on the website: the main treatment pages (detox, inpatient rehab, dual diagnosis) sit on a single-city web address that caps how widely they rank, well below what Glenville's authority could carry, and the site still has cleanup debris (duplicate web addresses, a stray phone-link pattern, thin auto-built pages, old migration files). Q2 plan: rewrite and open up the service pages so they rank across the Glenville area, run a full Google Business pass on the Glenville pin, refresh the top blog pages, and clean up the site. Tracking note: phone-call clicks still sit inside a generic click event (about 1,995 in 90 days, two to three times the form count), so adding click_phone_number and gmb_click as conversion events would let the dashboard show the true lead volume.

positives: Glenville leads its local Map Pack: #1 at the facility coordinate across the core addiction-treatment searches, and added 19 top-3 grid cells this period (improvement well ahead of any slippage).

Organic conversion rate roughly doubled across the post-recovery window (Q3 2025 0.39% to Q1 2026 0.94%). Form-submit leads held steady through the same window even as blog sessions softened, so each visit is doing more work.
Google Business and Maps clicks climbed from about 700 a month (Q4 2025 baseline) to a peak of 1,099 in March 2026: the local-search surface is absorbing more of the demand.
Maps clicks convert at 2.48% (29% of conversions from 6.2% of traffic), 5.8x the Google organic rate. This is the working channel.
Schema is already rich on the site (a global graph with MedicalOrganization, MedicalClinic, and MedicalProcedure), so the work is a refactor, not a rebuild.
Returning organic visitors convert at 1.71% (about 1.75x the new-visitor rate): the brand-pull to return-visit path is the highest-value flow.
A nearby competitor vacated the Glenville grid this period (down 197 cells), and Glenville absorbed part of the freed space.
OASAS Operating Certificate #10018, founded 1983, a 225-bed Glenville facility with a long operating history.
negatives: The main service pages are locked to -in-glenville-ny web addresses (pos 22-40 in Search Console, not in the top 100 for Albany, Saratoga, or Capital Region searches). Opening them up is the biggest on-site lever.
The Glenville Google Business link to the site has no tracking tag, so its Maps clicks cannot be told apart by location in GA4.
Cleanup debris: a stray tel: link pattern spawning dozens of indexed URLs, case-sensitive duplicate web addresses, and leftover WordPress migration files (old dated and author URLs) still indexed.
A batch of thin, auto-built suburb pages with keyword-stuffed addresses (several fail place-name validation) carry spam-policy risk and dilute the site.
Trust-signal layer is thin on the public site: no visible Joint Commission, CARF, or LegitScript, and no public insurance payor list. Competitors in the set show visible accreditation.
The brand engine carries most of the value (about half of clicks at a strong CTR), but a large block of older blog pages is losing rankings as informational search shifts to AI answers.

levers.name: Free up and rewrite the service pages
levers.why: The main service pages sit on -in-glenville-ny web addresses that lock them to one city. They rank pos 22-40 and are not in the top 100 for Albany, Saratoga, or wider Capital Region searches, even though the Glenville pin already owns the local map. Glenville dominates the location terms, so the next gains come from the treatment terms (detox, inpatient rehab, dual diagnosis). Opening up and rewriting these pages is the clearest on-site lever.

actions.name: Move the service pages off the -in-glenville-ny addresses to clean /services/ pages, with the proper redirects
Rewrite each service page around its treatment term, with the Glenville catchment as the area served
Wire internal links from the in-area pages into the service pages so intent routes to the right place
Add page-level structured data to each service page

levers.outcome: The service pages rank for the broader treatment searches across the Glenville area, not just the single-city term, and route visitors to the pages that book intakes.

levers.name: Site cleanup
levers.why: The site leaks the Maps win through cleanup debris: a stray tel: link pattern spawning indexed URLs, case-sensitive duplicate web addresses, a batch of thin auto-built suburb pages, and leftover WordPress migration files. Cleaning this up consolidates authority on the pages that matter and removes spam-policy risk.

actions.name: Consolidate the duplicate and near-duplicate pages with redirects to the right canonical page
Decide and execute on the thin auto-built suburb pages (keep, improve, or remove)
Fix the tel: link pattern and clear the leftover WordPress migration files
Refactor the structured data to page-level specifics instead of one global block everywhere

levers.outcome: Duplicate pages, the tel: pattern, and migration debris are cleared, the thin pages are resolved, and structured data is specific per page.

levers.name: Google Business depth on the Glenville pin
levers.why: HQDM manages the Glenville profile. A full profile pass closes the cleanest gaps: description, services list pointed at the real pages, attributes, a tracking tag on the website link so Maps clicks attribute by location, a regular posting cadence, and metadata on the photos already on the profile.

actions.name: Polish the Glenville description (credentials and Capital Region catchment)
Audit the services list and point each item at the matching service page
Complete the profile attributes and add a tracking tag to the website link
Keep a regular Posts cadence on the Glenville profile
Add keyword-relevant metadata to the photos already on the profile

levers.outcome: The Glenville profile is complete and consistent, and its Maps clicks attribute by location in GA4 for the first time.

levers.name: Off-page signal build
levers.why: Off-page work builds signal to the Glenville pin and its pages from outside, and does not need profile access. The SEO Neo / DAS / GBP Blast stack was removed in the 2026-05-13 program halt; this is the clean replacement: a citation buildout for Glenville, an embed stack, and a toxic-link disavow.

actions.name: Citation buildout for Glenville on foundational and vertical surfaces (SAMHSA, OASAS, BBB, Healthgrades, Psychology Today)
Embed stack for the Glenville pin
Pitch a contributed Capital Region byline to a behavioral-health outlet
Generate a toxic-link disavow file for client upload

levers.outcome: Glenville citations are live and consistent, the embed stack is in place, and a disavow file is ready for upload.

levers.name: Content refresh and trust signals
levers.why: The brand engine is the working surface (about half of clicks at a strong CTR), and the top high-impression blog pages are the highest-leverage refresh targets. The public trust-signal layer (Joint Commission, CARF, LegitScript, insurance payor list) is thin for a regulated vertical.

actions.name: Refresh the top blog pages (title, FAQ structured data, updated stats) and route them to the service pages
Pursue and surface the trust signals (accreditation badges and a public insurance payor list)
Q2 close-out: planned to executed to impact, per task

levers.outcome: The top blog pages hold their rankings and feed the service pages, the trust signals are documented and surfaced, and Q2 results are reported against the plan.
